pr_title: release-23.2: sqlstats: fix memory leak when writing statement insights and no transaction insights
pr_body:
Backport 1/1 commits from #122128

Backport 3/3 commits from #122699

/cc @cockroachdb/release

Release justification: bug fix

----

**sqlstats: delete sqlstats.StatsCollector interface**

There is one implementation of this interface. Let us
simply use the concrete type.

Epic: none

Release note: None

**sqlstats: introduce insights writer to StatsCollector**

This commit adds the insights writer to the `StatsCollector` struct. This
is in an effort to shift the responsibility of writing insights from being
owned by the `ssmemstorage.Container` to `sslocal.StatsCollector`. It makes
more sense for the StatsCollector, which is already responsible for
coordinating the writing of sql stats for a conn executor, to also
orchestrate insights collection operations. The sql stats application
container's intended purpose is to store per-application sql statistics.

Epic: none
Release note: None

**sqlstats,insights: use StatsCollector to record stmt insights**

This commit moves the recording of statement insights one layer up.
This decouples the writing of statement insights from the writing
of statement statistics to the sql stats containers. Previously,
if writing statement stats was throttled we also skipped writing
statement insights. The two processes may now occur independently.
Additionally, we introduce the flag `sendInsights` to the stats
collector, which is set at the start of every transaction. This
flag will be used to determine whether to observe insights for the
entire transaction. This ensures that writing statement insights
-> writing transaction insights so that the statement insight memory
will be freed.

Epic: none
Release note: None

**sqlstats,insights: use StatsCollector to record txn insights**

This commit moves the recording of transaction insights one layer up.
This decouples the writing of transaction insights from the writing
of transaction statistics to the sql stats containers. Previously,
if writing transaction stats was throttled we also skipped writing
transaction insights. This can lead to a memory leak if we've already
recorded statement insights for this transaction, as that memory is only
released once the corresponding transaction insight is sent. The two
processes may now occur independently.

This fixes a memory leak in the scenario where we continue to send
statement insights to the insights ingester without sending any
transaction insights. The ingester frees the memory used by statement
insights once it receives a transaction event. Previously, due to the
coupling of writing sql stats and insights, if we transaction stats
were throttled (e.g. due to in-memory capacities), we would start
accumulating statement insights.

Epic: none
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/121803
Release note: None

issue_context.title: sqlstats: leaking memory when throttling writing to in-memory sql stats
issue_context.body:
We have identified a memory leak in the sql stats sub system that can occur when we start throttling writing to in-memory transaction stats containers.

### Background
Insights system - tracks sql execution outliers. Note that for insights, there is an event ingestion process for which events sent from sql go from ingester -> registry -> insights store. This part of the system is omitted in this ticket for simplicity.
SQL Stats - tracks all execution stats, grouped by statement fingerprint (query shape) and other criteria.

### Memory leak
Both insights and sql stats are recorded at the end of stmt/txn execution respectively.
Below is the simplified recording process per stmt/txn - see corresponding functions for more details ([statement](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/a44e43c2815f091a6b6556f5d5bfcfa5032ecc77/pkg/sql/sqlstats/ssmemstorage/ss_mem_writer.go#L70), [transaction](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/a44e43c2815f091a6b6556f5d5bfcfa5032ecc77/pkg/sql/sqlstats/ssmemstorage/ss_mem_writer.go#L287))
```
	stats, created, throttled := s.getStatsWithKey(...) // will attempt to insert if key DNE

	if throttled {
		return ErrFingerprintLimitReached
	}

	// Collect the per-transaction statistics
	stats.Record(value)

 	s.insights.ObserveStatement(value) // or s.insights.ObserveTransaction when recording transaction
```

The memory leak occurs when we make calls to [ObserveStatement](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/feddaea233df5084fe023af9af210e63e8142486/pkg/sql/sqlstats/insights/registry.go#L38), which puts statement insight objects into a cache, without ever calling [ObserveTransaction](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/feddaea233df5084fe023af9af210e63e8142486/pkg/sql/sqlstats/insights/registry.go#L106), which is supposed to free that cache.

The above scenario occurs when we continue to record statement stats/insights but reach the in-memory transaction fingerprint threshold and start throttling transaction writes, meaning we skip `ObserveTransaction` in the above snippet.

### Reproduce
```
# disallowing the flush to be certain txn stats will always be full
set cluster setting sql.stats.flush.enabled = f;
set cluster setting sql.metrics.max_mem_txn_fingerprints = 10;
```
Observe the memory start to accumulate, tracing back to `RecordStatement`, where the statement insight is allocated.

### Fix
This memory leak will always occur if we call ObserveStatement with no ObserveTransaction.
A few things can be done:
- It seems that rather than this being an incremental process where we currenlty decide not to attempt to write to insights without also writing to sql stats, we should not couple these operations together. Insights has separate cluster settings controlling the limit on its in-memory cache.
- We could limit the number of statements written to the [insights registry](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/feddaea233df5084fe023af9af210e63e8142486/pkg/sql/sqlstats/insights/registry.go#L26) / do some memory accounting there 
- Ensure the statement insights are cleared at the end of each transaction execution. They are tracked in a sessionID -> statement insights map with the intention of being analyzed at the end of transaction execution, so it won't make sense to keep them around after the transaction ends since it is assumed that all statements belong to the same transaction. Addressing the first point in this list would ensure this happens.

Jira issue: CRDB-37559

Epic CRDB-37544
